problem: Text-to-image diffusion models are vulnerable to backdoor attacks that use fixed textual triggers and single-entity targets, making them susceptible to input defenses and detection methods.
approach: SemBD introduces representation-level triggers based on continuous semantic regions instead of discrete text patterns, implanted via distillation-based editing of cross-attention key-value matrices to enable semantically equivalent but textually diverse prompts to activate the backdoor.
contribution: Achieves 100% attack success rate while maintaining robustness against state-of-the-art input-level defenses through semantic regularization and multi-entity backdoor targets.

problem: LLM serving systems must balance high throughput and low latency across prefill and decode phases, where sharing GPUs causes performance interference while disaggregating wastes resources through model duplication and KV cache transfers.
approach: DuetServe dynamically activates SM-level GPU spatial multiplexing within a single GPU, using an attention-aware roofline model to forecast latency and an interruption-free execution engine to provide phase isolation only when contention threatens SLOs.
contribution: Improves total throughput by up to 1.3x while maintaining low generation latency compared to state-of-the-art frameworks.

problem: Graph neural network potentials like SchNet improve molecular dynamics accuracy but remain slower than classical force fields due to fragmented kernels and memory-bound pipelines that underutilize GPUs.
approach: FlashSchNet redesigns SchNet-style GNN-MD with four IO-aware techniques: flash radial basis fusing distance computation and basis expansion, flash message passing eliminating edge tensor materialization, flash aggregation via CSR segment reduce, and channel-wise 16-bit quantization of MLP weights.
contribution: Achieves 1000 ns/day aggregate simulation throughput over 64 parallel replicas on coarse-grained protein containing 269 beads, a 6.5x improvement.

problem: Learning sparse Gaussian graphical model structure from temporally correlated observations (single Glauber trajectory) is challenging because mixing-time-free guarantees are lacking and polynomial-time structure learning from sublinear samples is suspected computationally hard.
approach: The algorithm estimates conditional variances to reduce to unit-diagonal case, designs a local edge test extracting adjacency from short update windows by isolating pairwise influence, and aggregates statistics using robust median-based estimation.
contribution: First polynomial-time algorithm recovering conditional-independence graph from single Glauber trajectory with trajectory-length guarantee independent of mixing time.

problem: The Massart noise condition remains under-explored in emerging extensions of PAC learning theory beyond the classical framework, limiting understanding of sample complexity under this important interpolation regime.
approach: The work revisits transductive empirical risk minimization and derives sharper excess error bounds under Massart noise using offset Rademacher techniques and local metric entropy, then leverages this analysis for partial concept class learning.
contribution: Provides new sample complexity bounds for PAC learning with partial concept classes and completes the characterization of universal rates under Massart noise.

problem: Naive expansion of LLM-based multi-agent systems by adding new agents triggers performance collapse as the router cold-starts on heterogeneous and unreliable agents, limiting scalability.
approach: MonoScale proactively generates agent-conditioned familiarization tasks, harvests evidence from successes and failures, distills into natural-language memory to guide routing, and formalizes expansion as contextual bandit with trust-region memory updates.
contribution: Achieves stable performance gains as agent pool grows on GAIA and Humanity's Last Exam benchmarks, outperforming naive scale-up with monotonic non-decreasing performance guarantee under non-interfering expansion.

problem: Sub-bit model compression faces a fundamental one-bit wall because sign matrices resist low-rank approximation and appear random, yet most weights retain their initialization signs suggesting inherited randomness from initialization.
approach: Sign lock-in theory formalizes sign flip behavior under SGD as a stopping-time analysis showing geometric-tail distribution under bounded updates and rare re-entry conditions, enabling low-rank sign-template training from scratch.
contribution: Introduces from-scratch low-rank sign-template training method that prevents emergence of the one-bit wall bottleneck in sub-bit compression.

problem: Reasoning LLMs struggle with factuality in long-form settings, generating substantially more hallucinations than non-reasoning counterparts, while extending online RL for factuality poses challenges due to lack of reliable verification and reward hacking.
approach: Proposes a reward function simultaneously considering factual precision, response detail, and answer relevance, applied via online RL to learn high-quality factual reasoning while avoiding reward hacking pitfalls.
contribution: Achieves average 23.1 percentage points hallucination rate reduction with 23% increase in detail level and no helpfulness degradation across six long-form factuality benchmarks.

problem: Standard attention mechanisms use static token representations across all pair-wise computations, limiting representational alignment with diverse token-pair dynamics especially in multivariate time series with heterogeneous inter-channel dependencies.
approach: Prime attention modulates token representations for each token-pair to optimize each pair-wise interaction for that specific relationship, dynamically adjusting representations based on interaction type.
contribution: Achieves up to 6.5% improvement in forecasting accuracy across benchmarks and comparable performance using up to 40% less sequence length than standard attention.

problem: LLM-based retrieval systems are vulnerable to adversarial attacks, yet existing methods require known queries and victim model access, limiting validity of attacks in real-world query-agnostic black-box scenarios.
approach: Proposes query-agnostic black-box attack generating transferable injection tokens using zero-shot surrogate LLMs, establishes theoretical framework of LLMR, simulates attack as min-max problem with adversarial learning mechanism.
contribution: Demonstrates effective query-agnostic black-box attacks on benchmark datasets across popular LLM retrievers without victim queries or model knowledge.

problem: Generative VLA policies disregard spatiotemporal scale mismatch between cognition and action, leading to representation inefficiency and weak condition alignment during optimization.
approach: ResVLA shifts from generation-from-noise to refinement-from-intent paradigm, using spectral analysis to decouple control into deterministic low-frequency anchor (global intent) and stochastic high-frequency residual (local dynamics), anchoring generation on predicted intent.
contribution: Achieves competitive performance with strong robustness to language and embodiment perturbations, faster convergence than generative baselines, and strong real-world robot performance.

problem: Text-to-music diffusion models suffer from generation collapse to limited patterns and struggle to balance text alignment with diversity, as inference-time diversity control often harms text alignment by distorting prompt cues.
approach: PADS-TAL perturbs padding-indexed subspace while keeping non-padding conditioning fixed for controlled exploration, and introduces text-aware latent space aligning neighborhoods with text-implied genre structure for genre-consistent diversity.
contribution: Achieves 15.4% higher diversity at comparable text alignment and 71.6% improvement in within-genre diversity compared to prior perturbation methods.

problem: Test-time scaling in VLMs remains brittle because unstructured visual reasoning chains entangle perception and reasoning, leading to cascading errors from small perceptual mistakes and requiring expensive hand-crafted rewards.
approach: SPARC explicitly decouples visual perception from reasoning via two-stage pipeline with visual search localizing question-relevant regions followed by reasoning conditioned on those regions, enabling asymmetric compute allocation.
contribution: Improves Qwen3VL 4B on V* VQA by 6.7 points and surpasses visual-grounding approaches through independent test-time scaling of perception and reasoning stages.

problem: Existing model merging methods rely on fixed or manually tuned coefficients, making unified models sensitive to initial merging strategy and suboptimal for downstream adaptation.
approach: MetaMerging uses meta-learning to adaptively optimize merging coefficients by simulating adapter updates in inner loop and meta-optimizing coefficients in outer loop for task-specific adapter training.
contribution: Produces more balanced and generalizable unified models with strong performance across CV and NLP downstream tasks compared to parameter merging methods.

problem: Model pruning methods lack principled approaches to determine how many scored components can be discarded without sacrificing performance.
approach: EMP derives sparsity directly from importance score distribution using effective sample size (inverse Simpson index) from particle filtering, mapping scores to effective sample size and discarding lowest-scoring components.
contribution: Provides universal adaptive threshold with provable upper bound on loss change relative to original model across MLPs, CNNs, Transformers, LLMs, and KAN architectures.

problem: Formal complexity assessment of slice sampling for Dirichlet process models remains lacking because computational cost is random and potentially unbounded.
approach: Derives high-probability bounds on computational complexity of DP slice samplers showing that overhead from slice variables relative to cluster count is O_P(log n) uniformly across posterior regimes.
contribution: Establishes superlinear blow-ups in per-iteration cost occur with vanishing probability even in worst-case configurations, providing theoretical foundation for assessing DP slice sampler scalability.

problem: Vision-Language-Action models either generate actions autoregressively with poor performance or fragment information pathways through separate diffusion heads outside the backbone, limiting unified scalable architectures.
approach: Discrete Diffusion VLA discretizes action chunks and models them with discrete diffusion inside the unified transformer backbone, enabling adaptive decoding order and secondary re-masking for robust error correction.
contribution: Achieves 96.4% avg success on LIBERO, 71.2% visual matching on SimplerEnv-Fractal, 54.2% on SimplerEnv-Bridge with superior vision-language capability retention in out-of-distribution tests.

problem: Meta-RL typically assumes unobserved confounders can be excluded a priori, but real observational data from heterogeneous environments often contains confounding that violates this assumption.
approach: Employs partial identification methods to generate posterior counterfactual trajectories from candidate environments aligning with confounded observations, using these trajectories to find robust policy initialization.
contribution: Produces solution minimizing generalization loss in future inference tasks under confounded observational data across multiple environments.

problem: Existing Vision-Language-Action models for autonomous driving struggle with efficient inference and generalization to novel vehicle configurations and driving scenarios.
approach: Reasoning-VLA employs learnable action queries guided by predefined spatial representations and reasoning-enhanced vision-language features to generate continuous action trajectories in parallel, trained on consolidated standardized driving datasets with Chain-of-Thought reasoning.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art performance with strong generalization capability and excellent inference speed via parallel decoding across multiple driving benchmarks.

problem: Diffusion language models rely on heuristic random masking for pretraining that fails to target informative tokens, wasting computational effort on redundant or trivial tokens.
approach: InfoDLM reformulates mask selection as active feedback-driven process introducing Trainable Information-Gain signal to quantify masking information gain, develops feedback mechanism adapting masking policy to model state with maturity indicator.
contribution: Achieves up to 13% improvement in reasoning accuracy over LLaDA variant under comparable pretraining budgets through adaptive masking.

problem: Multimodal RAG pipelines treat visual inputs as static and immutable, failing on imperfect queries suffering from geometric distortions, quality degradation, or semantic ambiguity, leading to retrieval failures.
approach: V-QPP-Bench formulates visual query pre-processing as agentic decision-making where MLLMs autonomously diagnose imperfections and deploy perceptual tools to refine queries, enabling supervised fine-tuning.
contribution: Reveals critical vulnerabilities to visual imperfections and shows supervised fine-tuning enables compact models to achieve comparable or superior performance to larger proprietary models.

problem: Monocular-to-stereo conversion requires stereo inpainting of disocclusions but training-based methods rely on scarce stereo pairs or synthetic data with domain gaps.
approach: Proposes Geometric Reciprocity Theorem showing disocclusion mask when synthesizing target view equals mask of pixels lost warping from target to source, enabling self-supervised learning from monocular videos via cycle consistency.
contribution: First self-supervised framework for monocular-to-stereo conversion achieving improvements over training-free and supervised state-of-the-art methods.

problem: Dataset pruning remains underexplored for 3D modalities where class imbalance persists across training and test sets, forcing trade-offs between overall accuracy and mean accuracy across different evaluation priors.
approach: Casts pruning as quadrature approximation decomposing error into representation error and prior-mismatch bias, decouples likelihood from prior using distillation with calibrated teacher and geometry-preserving constraints, uses geometric embedding for robust pruning signals.
contribution: Framework elevates performance floor across diverse priors while offering flexibility for different evaluation preferences in 3D dataset pruning.

problem: Existing 4D human-object interaction generation focuses on global whole-body motion but fails to reason about part-level mechanics underlying interactions.
approach: HOI-PAGE explicitly reasons about part-level affordances using LLMs captured in part affordance graph representation, then generates 4D sequences optimizing for reference dynamics while satisfying part-level contact constraints.
contribution: Generates complex multi-object or multi-person interaction sequences with significantly improved realism and text alignment for zero-shot 4D HOI generation.

problem: Learning with sparse datasets and rich domain knowledge (expressed as logical rules and inequalities) requires enforcing hard constraints while existing neuro-symbolic methods only achieve soft penalty enforcement or non-differentiable post-processing.
approach: DisjunctiveNet represents rules as disjunctive constraints and applies hierarchical convex relaxations to obtain convex hull formulations enabling tractable linear constraints as differentiable optimization layers.
contribution: Achieves perfect rule satisfaction and strong predictive performance through end-to-end feasibility enforcement of hard input-dependent mixed-integer linear constraints.

problem: Discovering unknown one-parameter symmetry subgroups from data is challenging as conventional methods assume known symmetries.
approach: Proposes modular data-driven framework learning unknown functional mappings and discovering underlying symmetry subgroup by instantiating architectures with invariant/equivariant layers structured by Lie algebra, learning generator parameters end-to-end.
contribution: Identifies relevant continuous subgroups directly from data with guaranteed symmetry by construction across elliptic, hyperbolic, and parabolic regimes of matrix Lie groups including SO(n), SL(n), and Lorentz group.

problem: Low-Rank Adaptation employs shared low-rank updates across tokens, limiting ability to fully exploit adaptation subspace for tokens from different sequences.
approach: U-LoRA employs conditioned gating generating utilization coefficients along low-rank directions for each token, coordinates them using sequence-level context, and introduces bias-corrected exponential moving average historical prior for training stability.
contribution: Achieves competitive performance under comparable parameter budgets by better utilizing existing low-rank subspace via input-conditioned strategies without expanding it.

problem: Zero-shot imitation learning requires agents to reproduce expert behavior from single demonstrations without environment interaction or gradient updates at test time, making the multi-task inverse RL problem intractable.
approach: CIRL converts multi-task inverse RL into goal-inference problem using contrastive RL for maximum-entropy goal-conditioned policies, automatic goal proposal via GoalKDE, and mean-field variational model for amortized goal inference.
contribution: Consistently recovers demonstrator's intent by accounting for relative difficulty of reaching states, outperforming prior zero-shot imitation methods.

problem: Parallel agentic systems executing multiple teams independently perform overlapping computation on similar sub-problems, resulting in significant computational waste.
approach: LTS introduces global memory bank accessible to all teams and lightweight controller trained via stepwise RL deciding whether intermediate steps should be added, enabling selective cross-team information reuse.
contribution: Significantly reduces overall runtime while matching or improving task performance on AssistantBench and GAIA through learned memory admission.

problem: Cross-view geo-localization fails to generalize to unseen environments because contrastive learning treats all negatives equally, overrepressing semi-positive samples that share semantic cues and causing overfitting.
approach: Proposes uncertainty-aware framework using Deep Evidential Regression modeling Normal-Inverse-Gamma distribution to quantify environmental complexity, enabling adaptive softening of hard negatives in Soft InfoNCE.
contribution: Achieves 18% R@1 average improvement in zero-shot cross-dataset transfer compared to prior methods.

problem: Multimodal LLMs excel at offline understanding but struggle to serve as mobile assistants in continuous real-world audio-visual streams where responding at the right time is critical.
approach: PhoStream benchmarks streaming video, audio, and temporal reasoning with automated generative pipeline and realistic online inference pipeline, using LLM-as-a-Judge evaluation for open-ended responses.
contribution: Reveals temporal asymmetry where models excel on instant/backward tasks but sharply drop on forward tasks due to responding before required visual-audio cues appear.

problem: Sparse Johnson-Lindenstrauss transforms leverage random sparsity for computational efficiency but random sparsity leads to irregular memory access patterns that degrade GPU memory bandwidth utilization.
approach: FlashSketch pursues sketch-kernel co-design introducing BlockPerm-SJLT sparse sketches whose structure enables optimized CUDA kernel with tunable parameter trading GPU-efficiency against sketching robustness.
contribution: Achieves global geomean speedup of roughly 1.7x over prior GPU sketches while maintaining theoretical OSE framework guarantees.

problem: LLMs often hallucinate even with reference texts, especially when processing long contexts, as citations remain probabilistic output rather than foundation for generated content.
approach: Guidance builds structured fact pool of Prefix-Tail pairs from documents and uses lookahead strategy during decoding to predict intent, automatically replacing output with verified facts and citations when prefixes match.
contribution: Improves citation F1 score by 11.2% over state-of-the-art baselines with training-free approach pluggable into general or fine-tuned LLMs.

problem: Split federated learning suffers from biased optimization and unstable convergence under non-IID data because client information coordination lacks awareness of split architecture.
approach: BESplit exploits split architecture structure using Evidential Aggregation for fine-grained reweighting, Bias-Compensated Collaboration aligning split-layer representations via complementary pairing, and Dual-Teacher Distillation synchronizing knowledge.
contribution: Consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods in accuracy, convergence stability, and computational efficiency under diverse non-IID settings.

problem: Effective data selection for LLM pretraining is essential but existing approaches rely on external pretrained models or estimate importance from fixed model state, failing to capture dynamic data preference evolution.
approach: BLISS operates from scratch without external models using small proxy model and score model estimating importance through multi-step proxy updates, formalizing data selection as bilevel optimization.
contribution: Achieves 1.7x speedup reaching same performance as state-of-the-art method on 1B setting while delivering superior downstream performance on 410M/1B/2.8B models.

problem: Dynamic regret analysis for Follow-the-Regularized-Leader methods is less explored particularly for curved losses and adaptive optimizers like Adam.
approach: Builds on discounted-to-dynamic reduction with modular framework analyzing FTRL-related problems, applies to linear and logistic regression and Adam optimizers.
contribution: Simplifies proofs for optimal dynamic regret of online linear regression and yields new dynamic regret guarantees for online logistic regression and Adam.

problem: Knowledge editing in unified multimodal models shows striking modality gap where text-side efficacy reaches 92% but visual generation VQA accuracy is only 18.5%, suggesting edits fail to transfer cross-modality.
approach: Proposes Reasoning-augmented Parameter Editing explicitly activating edited knowledge before generation, improving VQA accuracy through activation of knowledge pathways for visual synthesis.
contribution: Demonstrates text-level knowledge edits do not guarantee reliable cross-modality transfer, motivates modality-aware editing methods with gains up to 18.6 percentage points.

problem: Stochastic variational inequality algorithms typically assume bounded variance or bounded domain, yet these assumptions are violated in problems like bilinear min-max with unbounded domains.
approach: Analyzes algorithms for solving monotone and structured nonmonotone VIs without bounded variance/domain assumptions, focusing on constrained settings allowing variance growth as squared norm of optimization variable.
contribution: Achieves oracle complexity of O-tilde(epsilon^-4) for making expected residual norm less than epsilon, best-known for constrained VIs.

problem: Reconstruction-based multimodal anomaly detection suffers from one-to-many crossmodal mapping problem where single 3D feature maps to multiple plausible RGB appearances, causing deterministic regression to over-smooth reconstructions.
approach: CFR learns bidirectional cyclic mappings for coarse reconstruction, identifies unreliable reconstructed features and selectively replaces them with high-confidence normal features to correct ambiguity-induced failures.
contribution: In 1-shot setting achieves 92.3 and 82.7 AUPRO at 30% FPR on MVTec 3D-AD and Eyecandies with 74.0 and 75.9 image-level AUROC scores.

problem: Scenario generation for autonomous driving tests either produces visually extreme crashes not physically feasible or overemphasizes controller-dependent aggressive maneuvers, missing the feasibility boundary band where scenarios are physically solvable but cause autonomy failures.
approach: ScenePilot formulates generation as constrained multi-objective RL combining RSS-derived physical-feasibility score with online-learned AV-risk predictor, introduces feasibility-aware shielding maintaining exploration near boundary.
contribution: Yields substantially higher collision rates (+6.2 pp) while preserving physical validity, with adversarial fine-tuning consistently reducing downstream crash rates.
